title: The Mystery of the Missing Rain
text: Have you ever wondered what happens to the rain after it falls? In some places, it rains only a few days a year, yet the people there never run out of water! How is this possible? Let's uncover the ancient secrets of water storage.

content.title: Think and Predict
content.description: If you lived in a desert with no rivers nearby and it only rained for one week a year, how would you make sure you have water for the rest of the year? Close your eyes and imagine a solution.

content.title: The Giant Water Bowl
content.description: Imagine a giant upside-down umbrella that catches every single drop of rain and funnels it into a safe, underground tank. People in the past built structures that worked exactly like this! One such structure is the Stepwell or Baoli.

title: Rainwater Harvesting & Baolis
text: The method of collecting and storing rainwater for future use is called Rainwater Harvesting. In ancient India, people built beautifully carved stepwells, known as Baolis or Vavs. Instead of drawing water up using a rope, people would walk down the steps to reach the water.

content.tip: Stepwells weren't just for storing water; they were also cool resting places for travelers during hot summer days!

content.question: What is the primary purpose of a Baoli (Stepwell)?
options: To provide a place for swimming
To store rainwater and allow people to walk down to it

title: Reflect on It
text: Explain in your own words why building steps down to the water was a better idea than using a bucket and rope in these specific regions. Can you think of any challenges they might have faced while building them?

title: Connecting the Dots
text: The idea of Baolis connects to modern-day Rainwater Harvesting systems on our rooftops! Just like the Baoli stored water underground, our modern homes catch rain on the roof and pipe it into tanks for summer use. It's the same ancient wisdom, just using new pipes!

content.title: Mini Project: Be a Water Detective
content.description: Look around your school or home. Can you find where the rainwater goes when it falls on the roof? Draw a simple map showing the path of a raindrop from the roof to the ground or drain.

content.mistake: Thinking that rainwater harvesting is a new, modern invention.
content.correction: It is an ancient practice! Kings and local communities built lakes, stepwells, and johads hundreds of years ago to save every drop of rain.
